hints: Look at what the chloride tells you, liquid covalent versus solid ionic is a big clue to metal or non-metal in Period 3.
A solid chloride that gives a neutral pH 7 solution points to NaCl, so Y is sodium, a typical metal.
Compare the pH 6 solid chloride with the liquid chloride to decide which one is still a metal and which one is a non-metal, then pick the good conductors.
walkthrough:
**Sort Period 3 chlorides by type**

Think like a detective. Metals make ionic solid chlorides, non-metals make covalent liquid or gaseous chlorides.

$$\text{metal + Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{solid ionic chloride} \quad , \quad \text{non-metal + Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{liquid covalent chloride}$$

**Identify X**

X gives a liquid product with chlorine, for example $\text{SiCl}_4$. That is covalent, so X is on the right side of Period 3, a non-metal like Si, P or S. Non-metals are poor conductors.

**Identify Y as sodium**

Y gives a solid chloride that dissolves to pH 7, neutral. That is classic $\text{NaCl}$:
$$\text{NaCl(s) + aq} \rightarrow \text{Na}^+\text{(aq) + Cl}^-\text{(aq), pH = 7}$$
No hydrolysis happens, so Y is Na, a Group 1 metal and an excellent conductor.

**Identify Z as magnesium**

Z gives a solid chloride that dissolves to pH 6, weakly acidic. That fits $\text{MgCl}_2$, where $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ slightly hydrolyses:
$$\text{[Mg(H}_2\text{O)}_6\text{]}^{2+} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{[Mg(H}_2\text{O)}_5\text{(OH)]}^+ + \text{H}_3\text{O}^+$$
So Z is Mg, also a metal and a good conductor. Therefore Y and Z conduct, X does not.

options.A: Incorrect because X is a non-metal. A liquid chloride means covalent bonding, so X cannot be a good electrical conductor even though Y (sodium) can.
options.B: Correct because Y is Na giving neutral NaCl solution and Z is Mg giving slightly acidic MgCl2 solution. Both Na and Mg are Period 3 metals with delocalised electrons, so both are good conductors.
options.C: Partly right but incomplete. Y alone (Na) is a good conductor, but it misses that Z (Mg) is also a metal. A pH 6 solution does not mean non-metal, Mg2+ hydrolysis gives weak acidity.
options.D: Incorrect because Z alone is not the full answer. Z (Mg) is a conductor, but Y (Na) is also a metal conductor with a neutral chloride solution, so both must be chosen.
